title: Ownership is lost once a stolen card passes through the thief's hand
summary: Zones follow control, so a stolen unit that is recalled goes to the thief's hand. The hand holds a bare card name, so when the thief replays it the new unit's owner defaults to the playing seat, and the engine records the thief as owner. The rulings say ownership never moves ("its OWNER's, always, forever"). The verifier's probe measured owner = thief after the replay. Low impact today because zones follow control, but the owner field no longer means what the ruling says it keeps meaning. (Measured by a verifier probe; the probe files are not committed.)

**2. Ownership does not move. Only the destination does.**

closed: fixed on 2026-10-22 (CT-233): a stolen card keeps its owner through the thief's own hand, bin and cache (551); the routes still open are F-U01-6.

title: The engine lets effects reach the stack and the bins across regions
summary: The rules make the stack, the bins and the caches regional (Manual p.19, Caleb, the owner ruling of 2026-10-11 (“The stack, the bins and the…”)): each region has its own stack, shared by the players present in it, and a player's bin and cache can be reached only where that player is present. The engine keeps one stack for battle and offers a stack item and the cards in either bin as targets from every region, so Frosted Denial, Woodland Warding and Molten Riftbreaker reach across regions. Cache targets already agree (owner ruling of 2026-09-05, “A cached card is a target…”). Unit targeting, statics and triggers are region-scoped and agree with print. (Measured by a verifier probe, not committed, and by the 414 CR test.)

Every single effect is specific to the region it takes

closed: fixed on 2026-10-22 (CT-234): each region has its own stack and a bin is reached only where its player is present; 578 drives Molten Riftbreaker at home and in the battle, and the bin reach.

title: Ownership is lost when a card passes through a hand or bin
summary: Hands and bins store bare card names, so a stolen unit that is recalled to the thief's hand (owner ruling of 2026-08-30, “zones follow control, in all four…”) and played again becomes a new entity owned by the thief. The owner ruling of 2026-08-29 (“Cosmic Reversal reaches the board; every…”) and the owner ruling of 2026-08-30 (“zones follow control, in all four…”) say ownership never moves ('its OWNER's, always, forever'; in constructed the owner is whoever brought the card). (Measured by a verifier probe; the probe files are not committed.)

title: The engine's stack and bin effects reach across regions
summary: Card code that iterates g.s.stack (for example Molten Riftbreaker's 'negate all allied spells') has no region filter. An effect resolving in one region negated a spell on the stack in another region. The designer says everything in the game is region specific. The owner ruling of 2026-08-29 (“Cosmic Reversal reaches the board; every…”) and the owner ruling of 2026-08-30 (“An ally includes itself, "another" is…”) kept the stack global on purpose; the owner ruling of 2026-10-11 (“The stack, the bins and the…”) (the owner, 2026-10-11) amends both, so this is an engine divergence to fix (CT-234). (Measured by a verifier probe; the probe files are not committed.)

title: The engine has one stack for every region: an effect in one region reaches a stack item in another
summary: Cosmic Reversal's stack half (and Molten Riftbreaker, Frosted Denial) iterate the whole stack regardless of region, as the owner ruling of 2026-08-29 (“Cosmic Reversal reaches the board; every…”) and the owner ruling of 2026-08-30 (“An ally includes itself, "another" is…”) had it before the owner ruling of 2026-10-11 (“The stack, the bins and the…”) made the stack regional. The designer says everything in the game is region specific and nothing crosses regions except attacking. Probe: Cosmic Reversal resolving in A's home region recalled A's Luminous Arc from the battle region's stack.

title: Three routes still give a card the wrong owner: a mod applied from hand, bin or cache, an inline-played spell that resolves into a bin, and effects that move a bin card to a hand
summary: The rule (owner 2026-10-22, "Reset in shared zones") keeps a card's owner through a player's own hand, bin and cache. The engine fixed the main routes in the 2026-10-22 round (CT-233, guard 551), and its own report lists three it did not: a mod applied from a hand, bin or cache takes the player applying it as its owner (the mod's owner field also means who applied it); a spell played inline that resolves or fizzles into a bin loses its owner; and card effects that move a bin card to a hand pass no owner. Filed as new tickets by that round; not re-measured here.

evidence.quote: CR 102.4 / CT-233: a stolen card recalled to the thief hand and played again is still its owner card

closed: fixed on 2026-10-24 (CT-343, CT-344): a mod keeps its card's owner apart from who applied it (622), and every bin exit and stack-to-hand recall passes the owner (623, 624); an inline-played spell already carried it.

title: A foreign-owned card recalled from a bin to a hand loses its owner
summary: Rule: moving a card out of a bin into a hand keeps its owner. Engine: Eldritch Reclaimer (and the other bin->hand recalls that call toHand without opts.owner, plus Cosmic Reversal stack->hand) drops the PlayerState.foreign entry, so the thief becomes the owner. Probe zz-probe-U01-1 fails on it. Probably the known F-U01-6.
closed: fixed on 2026-10-24 (CT-344): Eldritch Reclaimer and the other bin-to-hand recalls take the card with takeFromBin and pass its owner to the hand (623 class guards).
